passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: • Significant subsequent events General facts on Nokia Financial statements Other information Significant subsequent events Nokia to operate with two primary operating segments Nokia announced on 19 November 2025, together with its new strategy, that it will reorganize its business into two primary operating segments to better align to customer needs and accelerate innovation as the AI supercycle increases demand for advanced connectivity. This reorganization took effect as of 1 January 2026. The reorganization recognizes Network Infrastructure as a growth segment, positioned to capitalize on the rapid, global AI and data center build-out while continuing to innovate for its telecommunications customer base. The segment consists of three business units Optical Networks, IP Networks and Fixed Networks and is led by David Heard. The new Mobile Infrastructure segment brings together Nokia’s Core Networks portfolio, Radio Networks portfolio and Technology Standards (formerly Nokia Technologies). It is positioned for core and radio network technology and services leadership to lead the industry to AI-native networks and 6G. The new segment brings together a portfolio whose value creation is founded on mobile communication technologies based on 3GPP standards with a strong cash flow position underpinned by IP licensing. It is led by Justin Hotard on an interim basis and consists of three business units Core Software, Radio Networks and Technology Standards. In addition, as part of its strategy work, Nokia identified several units which are not seen as core to the future of the company’s strategy. These units were moved into a dedicated operating segment called Portfolio Businesses while the company assesses the best value creating opportunity for them. The units moved were: ▪ Fixed Wireless Access CPE (previously in Fixed Networks in Network Infrastructure) ▪ Site Implementation and Outside Plant (previously in Fixed Networks in Network Infrastructure) ▪ Enterprise Campus Edge (previously in Cloud and Network Services) ▪ Microwave Radio (previously in Mobile Networks) 114 Nokia Annual Report on Form 20-F 2025 General facts on Nokia American Depositary Shares 115 Controls and procedures 115 Government regulation 116 Sales in United States-sanctioned countries 116 Taxation 117 Key ratios 120 Alternative performance measures 121 115 Nokia Annual Report on Form 20-F 2025 Contents Business overview Corporate governance Operating and financial review and prospects General facts on Nokia • American Depositary Shares • Controls and procedures Government regulation Sales in United States- sanctioned countries Taxation Key ratios Alternative performance measures Financial statements Other information American Depositary Shares Fees and charges ADS holders may have to pay the following service fees to the Depositary : Service Fees, USD Issuance of ADSs Up to 5 cents per ADS (1) Cancellation of ADSs Up to 5 cents per ADS (1) Distribution of cash dividends or other cash distributions Up to 2 cents per ADS Distribution of ADSs pursuant to (i) stock dividends, free stock distributions or (ii) exercises of rights to purchase additional ADSs Up to 5 cents per ADS

credit_strengths.text: The issuer holds a net cash position, with cash and short-term investments exceeding reported borrowings, so gross leverage sits only modestly above the sector median and the indicative financial risk profile is minimal on a net-debt basis.

Operating cash flow covers dividends and buybacks combined comfortably, leaving a meaningful buffer after shareholder distributions; this internal cash generation, not balance-sheet drawing, funds the capital returns programme.

key_risks.text: Operating income fell sharply year on year and the operating margin is far below the sector median, so the earnings base supporting interest and distributions has thinned materially; the reorganization into two primary segments adds execution risk during the transition.

Interest coverage has roughly halved year on year and sits well below the sector median, while EBITDA coverage is also weaker than peers; the disclosed finance cost line is the binding constraint on debt service headroom rather than leverage itself.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Cash flow to debt is in line with the sector median but slightly below the prior year, and the current ratio is modestly below peers, indicating adequate but not superior liquidity relative to the sector; the ratio remains above one.

Free cash flow and its coverage of debt cannot be assessed because capital expenditure is not separately tagged, so the analyst cannot confirm that distributions are funded from free cash flow rather than operating cash flow alone; this gap is material to the view.

overall_credit_view.text: The credit profile is anchored by net cash and a minimal indicative financial risk profile, with borrowings declining over the trend period; leverage is close to the sector median and the Altman zone is safe, supporting a stable view absent a further earnings deterioration.

The offsetting concern is earnings quality: margins and interest coverage are well below sector medians and trending down, so the analyst judges that debt service headroom depends on restoring operating profitability rather than on the current balance-sheet cushion.

credit_strengths.text: 發行人持有淨現金狀況，現金及短期投資超過所報告的借款，因此總槓桿僅略高於行業中位數，而按淨債務基準計算的指示性財務風險狀況為極低。
經營現金流可舒適地覆蓋股息與回購的總和，在股東分派後仍留有可觀緩衝；此內部現金產生（而非動用資產負債表）為資本回報計劃提供資金。

key_risks.text: 經營收入按年大幅下降，經營利潤率遠低於行業中位數，因此支撐利息與分派的盈利基礎已實質性削弱；重組為兩個主要分部在過渡期間增加了執行風險。
利息覆蓋率按年大致減半，且遠低於行業中位數，而 EBITDA 覆蓋率亦弱於同業；所披露的財務成本項目（而非槓桿本身）是債務償付空間的約束因素。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 現金流對債務比率與行業中位數一致，但略低於上一年度，而流動比率略低於同業，表明流動性相對於行業為足夠但非優越；該比率仍高於一。
自由現金流及其對債務的覆蓋無法評估，因為資本開支未單獨標記，因此分析師無法確認分派是由自由現金流（而非僅經營現金流）提供資金；此缺口對觀點具重大影響。

overall_credit_view.text: 信用狀況以淨現金及極低的指示性財務風險狀況為錨，借款在趨勢期內下降；槓桿接近行業中位數，且 Altman 區域為安全，支持在盈利未進一步惡化的情況下維持穩定觀點。
抵銷性的關注點是盈利質量：利潤率與利息覆蓋率遠低於行業中位數且呈下降趨勢，因此分析師判斷債務償付空間取決於恢復經營盈利能力，而非取決於當前資產負債表緩衝。
